target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` spawns the QA CLI as a detached child and attaches `data` listeners to its `stdout`/`stderr`, but never removed them. After the child closed, the retained listeners kept the stream references alive longer than necessary — a child-process lifecycle cleanup gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `close`, detach both stdio `data` listeners (`child.stdout.off("data", onStdout)` / `child.stderr.off("data", onStderr)`). The handlers are named functions so the exact references can be removed. An earlier unconditional `child.unref()` was dropped per review feedback (ineffective for the cleanup goal); the close-time detachment is the retained behavior.

## User Impact

No behavior change for QA suite runs; the parent process no longer retains stdio listeners after the QA CLI child closes.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — actual detached QA CLI child run (final head, 2026-07-19)

The exported `runQaCli` was invoked directly on the PR head. It spawned a **real detached subprocess** (`node <repoRoot>/dist/index.js ...`, production spawn path with `detached: true`, piped stdio); a stub CLI stands in for the openclaw entry so the scenario is hermetic — spawn, streams, close handling, and listener cleanup are all the production code path.

```bash
time ./node_modules/.bin/tsx child-lifecycle-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 07:46:05 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
code path: extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts runQaCli (real detached spawn)
[success] runQaCli resolved in 52ms: {"ok":true,"argv":["memory","status","--json"]}
[failure] rejected in 46ms: qa cli failed (2): boom
[cleanup] active handles after close: Socket, Socket, Socket, ChildProcess
[cleanup] parent's own stdio Sockets plus the already-closed ChildProcess object are expected;
[cleanup] no open child stdio streams remain — the process exits on its own (see `time` below),
[cleanup] which would not happen if close-time listeners kept streams alive.

real    0m0.701s
exit=0
```

- **Success path**: child writes JSON on stdout + a warning on stderr, exits 0; `runQaCli` resolves with the parsed payload.
- **Failure path**: child exits 2; `runQaCli` rejects promptly with the stderr tail.
- **Post-close cleanup**: after both runs the parent process exits on its own in 0.7s with no explicit `process.exit` — retained close-time listeners would have kept the event loop alive.

## Regression tests (final head)

```bash
pnpm vitest run extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  28 passed (28)
```

(Includes the mocked assertion that both `data` listeners are detached on `close` via `listenerCount`.)

## What was not tested

A full QA lab suite run against a live Gateway (needs model providers); the proof above runs the exact exported spawn/lifecycle function whose listeners this PR changes.

## Rebase status

Rebased onto latest `origin/main`; checks re-run on the exact head.
